provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Lets a feeling well up over something the speaker takes as a truth of the world: how fast the years go, how outrageous someone is (月日が経つのは早いもんだ). Its siblings are the social norm stated as advice (早く寝るもんだ) and the excuse-making reason at the end of a clause (だって寒いんだもん). It follows plain forms, past included (よく言ったもんだ), and よく(も) often sets it up.

examples.ruby: あれからもう十年[じゅうねん]、月日[つきひ]が経[た]つのは早[はや]いもんだ。
examples.english: Ten years already since then — time really does fly, doesn't it.

examples.ruby: よくもあんな大[おお]きな荷物[にもつ]を担[かつ]いで運[はこ]べるもんだ。
examples.english: The nerve — how does he even lift a load that size and haul it around?

examples.ruby: 人[ひと]の縁[えん]というのは、思[おも]わぬところでつながるもんだ。
examples.english: It's funny how people's paths end up crossing in the least expected places.

patterns.usage_note: Passes a verdict on a state or quality, whether gratitude, sarcasm, or exasperation: ありがたいこった, 難儀なこった, ご苦労なこった. It usually follows an evaluative i-adjective, or a na-adjective or noun plus な, and is a clipped ことだ heard in gruff colloquial speech and in fiction that evokes it. The sibling lane gives the listener advice (自分で言うこった) and follows a plain non-past verb.

examples.ruby: みんな無事[ぶじ]に戻[もど]ってきて、ありがたいこった。
examples.english: Everyone made it back in one piece — thank heaven for that.

examples.ruby: 五年[ごねん]も音沙汰[おとさた]なしとは、水臭[みずくさ]いこった。
examples.english: Not a word out of him in five years — that's cold of him, that is.

examples.ruby: 傘[かさ]を忘[わす]れた日[ひ]に限[かぎ]って土砂降[どしゃぶ]りとは、ひどいこった。
examples.english: Pouring buckets on the one day I leave my umbrella at home — that's rough, that is.

patterns.usage_note: Rhetorical exclamation of degree: with どんなに, どれほど, or なんと in front, it says the degree is past measuring, and no answer is expected despite the question shape (どんなに待ちわびていたことか). Where もんだ marvels at a general truth, ことか measures the speaker's own feeling, typically inward and common in writing and soliloquy. ことだろう／ことでしょう is a softer, more speculative variant, often about someone else's feeling.

examples.ruby: この日[ひ]をどんなに待[ま]ちわびていたことか。
examples.english: You have no idea how long I'd been waiting for this day.

examples.ruby: あの一言[ひとこと]がどれほど嬉[うれ]しかったことか。
examples.english: You've no idea how happy that one remark made me.

examples.ruby: 一人[ひとり]で暮[く]らす娘[むすめ]を、毎晩[まいばん]どんなに案[あん]じていることか。
examples.english: Every night I worry about my daughter living on her own — more than words can say.

patterns.usage_note: An exclamation at something just noticed: on a falling tone the negative question asks nothing and becomes surprise, discovery, or praise at what the speaker has taken in (鍵はここにあるじゃないか, 君に似合うじゃないか). The sibling lane is the rhetorical question that presses an obvious point onto the hearer, typically as reproach (確認すると言ったじゃないか). Bare か reads as blunt and masculine; じゃないですか is the polite shape.

examples.ruby: その帽子[ぼうし]、なかなか君[きみ]に似合[にあ]うじゃないか。
examples.english: Hey, that hat actually suits you rather well.

examples.ruby: 初[はじ]めてなのに、ちゃんと一人[ひとり]で作[つく]れたじゃないか。
examples.english: First time trying and you made it all by yourself — nice work!

examples.ruby: さんざん探[さが]し回[まわ]ったのに、鍵[かぎ]はここにあるじゃないか。
examples.english: After all that hunting around — the key was right here!

patterns.usage_note: Voices a feeling half to oneself — admiration, resignation, wistfulness — on a plain-form sentence, often lengthened to なあ (ここの海はきれいだな). It is more inward than ね, which hands the thought to a listener, and gentler than よ, which presses information on one. After a dictionary-form verb the same syllable is also the prohibitive な (行くな 'don't go'), which is clipped and sharply falling.

examples.ruby: 三年[さんねん]ぶりに来[き]たけど、ここの海[うみ]はきれいだな。
examples.english: First time back in three years — the sea here really is beautiful.

examples.ruby: 今夜[こんや]中[じゅう]に片[かた]づけるには、この量[りょう]はさすがに多[おお]いな。
examples.english: If I'm supposed to clear this by tonight, this really is too much.

examples.ruby: この坂[さか]を自転車[じてんしゃ]で登[のぼ]るのは、やっぱりきついな。
examples.english: Cycling up this hill really is rough, no two ways about it.

patterns.usage_note: Tints a statement with the speaker's own felt reaction — mild surprise, dismay, or quiet resolve — arrived at through their own experience (財布を家に置いてきたわ). Rising わ is the stereotyped feminine register, now fiction-flavored rather than everyday Tokyo speech; falling わ is ordinary Kansai speech used by men and women alike. Unlike ね it asks for no agreement, and unlike よ it presses nothing on the listener.

examples.ruby: うっかりして、財布[さいふ]を家[いえ]に置[お]いてきたわ。
examples.english: Oh no — I've gone and left my wallet at home.

examples.ruby: まあ、庭[にわ]のばらがこんなに見事[みごと]だわ。
examples.english: My, the roses in the garden are absolutely splendid.

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]の相手[あいて]は、思[おも]ったより手強[てごわ]いわ。
examples.english: Today's opponent is tougher than I bargained for, I must say.
